title: REQ-20261103-OPS001 — Binding death benefit nomination as lodged: one witness only, not valid as binding (Priya Natarajan → Arjun Mehta 100%)
content:
Caldova binding death benefit nomination (lapsing) form lodged with Priya Natarajan's application pack for Caldova Super (Select) CS-2049817.

Form as received: signed and dated by the member on 30 Oct 2026. Nominee: Arjun Mehta — relationship stated as de facto partner (living together since 2021) — 100% of the death benefit. Witness 1: Hannah Lewis (adviser; over 18; not named in the nomination) — signed and dated 30 Oct 2026, witness declaration completed. Witness 2: section left blank — no name, signature, date or declaration.

Assessment (Benefits & Eligibility; trust deed TD 9.3 and TD 9.5; SIS reg 6.17A): a binding nomination must be signed and dated by the member in the presence of TWO witnesses, each aged 18 or over and not named in the nomination, and each must sign a witness declaration. With only one witness the form does not meet the requirements, so it is NOT valid as a binding nomination. Everything else is in order: a de facto partner is a SIS dependant, so Arjun is an eligible nominee, and the share totals 100%.

Treatment: Caldova records the form as a non-binding nomination (Arjun Mehta 100%). If Priya died before a valid binding nomination is lodged, the trustee would decide who receives her benefit and would take the non-binding nomination into account as an indication of her wishes. The account opening is not delayed.

Action (adviser update to Hannah Lewis): Priya to sign a new Caldova BDBN form in front of two adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries — Arjun cannot be a witness — with both witnesses completing their declarations at the same sitting. Once accepted, the nomination is binding for 3 years from the date it is signed and must then be renewed.

Plain-English wording for Priya: 'We've recorded your nomination for Arjun as your wishes. To make it binding on the trustee, it needs to be signed again in front of two adult witnesses who aren't named in it — your adviser can help you with this.'
